properties.name: Pilot - Eradication of buckthorn
properties.description: A pilot project to eliminate buckthorn from natural areas in Pointe-Claire parks.
properties.project_area: Terra Cotta Park, Tony-Proudfoot Park, Cedar Park Heights Park, David-W-Beck Park, and the green space between Kings and Queens Avenues
actions: Cutting buckthorn plants.
Treating stumps with a naturally occurring pathogenic fungus to prevent regrowth.
Manually removing and sterilizing stumps, then installing a plastic membrane to block regrowth.
Inspecting the sites annually and manually removing remaining shoots.
Planting a diversity of native trees and plants to restore the area.
properties.marker_location: Marker shows the organization's location, not the project sites.

properties.name: Phytotechnology station for invasive plant management
properties.description: A phytotechnology station uses native plants and floating islands to help limit the establishment of invasive plants.
actions: Established a riparian strip with diverse native plants to compete with invasive plants and filter runoff.
Installed floating plant islands to make it harder for invasive plants that need sunlight to establish.
properties.marker_location: Marker shows the project location at the Montréal Botanical Garden.

properties.name: Invasive plant control — Parc-nature du Cap-Saint-Jacques
properties.description: The City is controlling invasive alien plants in the Embouchure sector using tarps and annual follow-ups.
actions: Tarps are installed over periwinkle colonies.
Annual monitoring maintains the tarps and removes regrowth; tarps are planned to remain for two years.
properties.marker_location: Approximate point within Parc-nature du Cap-Saint-Jacques; exact treatment area is not mapped.

properties.name: Buckthorn control — Parc-nature du Bois-de-Liesse
properties.description: A pilot project in the Champs sector tests a specific cutting technique to control buckthorn.
actions: Control buckthorn using a specific cutting technique.
properties.marker_location: Approximate point in the Saint-Laurent portion of Parc-nature du Bois-de-Liesse; exact treatment area is not mapped.

properties.name: Japanese knotweed control — Parc-nature du Bois-de-Saraguay
properties.description: Tarps and annual follow-ups are used to control Japanese knotweed in the Sentier Polo sector.
properties.project_area: Parc-nature du Bois-de-Saraguay — Sentier Polo sector
actions: Tarps are installed over Japanese knotweed colonies.
Annual monitoring maintains the tarps and controls regrowth; tarps are planned to remain for at least six years.
properties.marker_location: Approximate point within Parc-nature du Bois-de-Saraguay; exact treatment area is not mapped.

properties.name: Invasive plant control — Parc-nature de la Pointe-aux-Prairies
properties.description: The City is carrying out invasive plant control in the Bois-de-la-Réparation, River, and Marais sectors.
properties.species_note: Buckthorn is also mentioned in the Bois-de-la-Réparation sector; species not identified.
actions: Bois-de-la-Réparation: manually remove buckthorn plants, cut and encapsulate large specimens, manually remove garlic mustard from April to June, and bend common reed plants.
River and Marais: install tarps over Japanese knotweed colonies and monitor annually to maintain tarps and control regrowth; tarps are planned to remain for at least six years.
properties.marker_location: Approximate point within Parc-nature de la Pointe-aux-Prairies; exact treatment area is not mapped.

properties.name: Common reed control — Parc Frédéric-Back
properties.description: The City is controlling common reed in the Boisé and Plaine sectors and restoring treated areas with native plants.
properties.project_area: Parc Frédéric-Back — Boisé and Plaine sectors
actions: Install tarps over common reed colonies and inspect them annually.
Maintain tarps and control regrowth around their perimeter for two to three years.
Seed and plant native species in treated areas.
properties.marker_location: Approximate point within Parc Frédéric-Back; exact treatment area is not mapped.

properties.name: Invasive plant control — Parc du Mont-Royal
properties.description: The City is controlling several invasive plants in the Flanc Sud and Sommet sectors.
properties.project_area: Parc du Mont-Royal — Flanc Sud and Sommet sectors
actions: Manually remove buckthorn and alder buckthorn; cut and encapsulate large specimens.
Manually remove young Norway maples and cut large specimens.
Cover Virginia creeper plants with tarps.
properties.marker_location: Approximate point within Parc du Mont-Royal; exact treatment area is not mapped.

properties.name: Bringing Resilient and Biodiversity-Rich Forests Back — Bois-de-Saraguay
properties.organization: Ville de Montréal / Nature-Action Québec / Collège Saint-Laurent / Centre d'étude de la forêt / MELCCFP
properties.description: One of two sites in Montréal's forest-restoration initiative, which addresses buckthorn invasion and restores diverse, resilient forest ecosystems.
properties.species_note: Glossy and common buckthorn are discussed; the species targeted at this site is not identified.
actions: The forest-restoration initiative controlled buckthorn rather than aiming for eradication.
Across the initiative, a forestry mulcher crushed and dislodged stumps and buckthorn root systems; site-specific use is not identified.
Diverse native species were planted to restore forest structure and resilience.
properties.marker_location: Approximate point within Parc-nature du Bois-de-Saraguay; exact intervention area is not mapped.

properties.name: Domaine Saint-Paul forest rehabilitation
properties.description: A forest rehabilitation project following ash-tree removals at Domaine Saint-Paul. The 2025 update reports more than 1,500 buckthorn plants removed and 58% of planned trees and shrubs planted.
actions: Remove invasive buckthorn plants as part of forest rehabilitation.
Plant trees and shrubs to restore the site; the 2025 update reported 58% of planned planting complete.
Carry out habitat improvements, including wildlife structures, and renovate boardwalks.
The related forestry intervention removed dead or declining ash trees near trails and infrastructure during winter 2024–2025.
properties.marker_location: Approximate point within Domaine Saint-Paul; exact rehabilitation area is not mapped.

properties.name: Phragmites removal at Lac des Battures
properties.organization: L’Île des fleurs / Nature-Action Québec / Borough of Verdun
properties.description: A volunteer phragmites-removal activity supporting shoreline biodiversity zones established by Nature-Action Québec. The activity also helped maintain trees and shrubs planted in fall 2024.
actions: Manually remove invasive phragmites, then bag and carry away the removed plant material.
Maintain trees and shrubs planted along the lakeshore in fall 2024.
properties.marker_location: Approximate point at Lac des Battures; volunteer work took place along the lakeshore.

properties.name: Asian knotweed control - Ile Haynes
properties.organization: Comité ZIP Jacques-Cartier / Ville de Montréal
properties.description: A multi-year project to control invasive knotweeds and restore natural areas in the Ile Haynes sector.
actions: Cut knotweed above ground and remove roots and rhizomes.
Cover treated ground with a tarp to limit regrowth.
Monitor the sites for three years and plant native species during the final project phases.
properties.marker_location: Approximate point on Ile Haynes representing the project area; treatment sites are not individually mapped.

properties.name: Woodland Guardians - Volunteer Thursdays
properties.description: Weekly volunteer activities supporting biodiversity in a Mercier-Ouest woodland, including invasive-plant removal, trail maintenance, planting, and site cleanups.
actions: Remove invasive plants, including buckthorn, vine, garlic mustard, and Anthriscus.
Maintain trails, prune trees and shrubs, clean the site, and plant perennials and shrubs as needed.
properties.marker_location: Approximate point in Mercier-Ouest representing the activity area; individual woodland work sites are not mapped.

Contact the Green Line at 514-684-3114 or LigneVerte@DDO.qc.ca.

properties.name: Bateliers and de la Merci parks - invasive plant removal
properties.description: A borough contract to restore the wooded areas of two riverside parks: removing invasive plants, planting native trees and shrubs, and working toward protected-area status for Bateliers Park.
properties.species_note: Schubert cherry (an ornamental chokecherry cultivar) was also removed.
properties.project_area: Parc des Bateliers and Parc de la Merci, Ahuntsic-Cartierville, Montreal
actions: Removing invasive plants (about 90,000 stems over almost two hectares in 2016).
Planting native species (nearly 185 trees and over 500 shrubs in 2016).
Adding interpretive panels, bird nesting boxes and feeders, and bat roosts.
Maintaining the sites over five years, with Bateliers Park to become a protected area.
properties.marker_location: Marker shows Parc des Bateliers; Parc de la Merci is just to the east.
